mathgap.title: Signed 'has more than' interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret any phrase of the form 'X has more than Y' as a signed difference X − Y = N, preserving the order presented.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement directly says that one person has more tomatoes than another.
mathgap.example: Treating 'Rubi has 3 more tomatoes than Amelia' as an absolute count rather than the signed difference Rubi − Amelia = 3.

mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: When a transfer 'X gives N to Y' occurs, subtract N from X and add N to Y, updating each person's count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For every statement describing a give/receive transfer of tomatoes.
mathgap.example: Applying 'Nigel gives 6 tomatoes to Thurston' by adding 6 to Nigel instead of subtracting.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Introduce a distinct variable for each person and translate every relevant statement into a linear equation, then solve the system.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After all tomato‑related statements have been identified and expressed as equations.
mathgap.example: Listing equations but never solving them, leaving the answer undetermined.

mathgap.title: Signed difference phrasing
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'difference between X and Y' as the signed difference X − Y, preserving the order presented.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement refers to the difference between two people's tomato counts.
mathgap.example: Reading 'the difference between Nealie and Pinkie' as |Nealie − Pinkie| instead of Nealie − Pinkie.

mathgap.title: Include transfers as constraints before solving relational equations
mathgap.principle: Apply all transfer statements first, updating each person's count, and then use those updated counts in relational equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Immediately after parsing all transfer statements, before handling any difference or 'has more than' equations.
mathgap.example: Solving relational equations using the original counts and ignoring the net effect of transfers.

mathgap.title: Direct counts as initial constraints
mathgap.principle: Treat statements that give an explicit count (e.g., 'X has N items') as the initial amount before any transfers.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement provides an exact tomato count for a person.
mathgap.example: Assuming 'Gloria has 7 tomatoes' is the final count after transfers, instead of the starting count.

mathgap.title: Answer formatting
mathgap.principle: Output the final answer using the exact required format: 'The final answer is \boxed{<integer>}'.
mathgap.example: Writing 'The answer is 5' instead of the required boxed format.

mathgap.title: Direct counts with transfers
mathgap.principle: Treat explicit count statements as describing the initial amount before any transfers. After applying transfers, update counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When both a direct count and later transfer statements involve the same person.
mathgap.example: Using a direct count as the final amount and then also adding a transfer to it, double‑counting the tomatoes.

mathgap.title: Aggregate multiple transfers per person
mathgap.principle: Sum all incoming and outgoing transfer amounts for each person to obtain a net change, then apply them.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a person appears in more than one transfer statement.
mathgap.example: Applying each transfer separately and forgetting to combine them, leading to an incorrect net total.

mathgap.title: Complete system solving
mathgap.principle: After translating all constraints into linear equations, actually solve the system (or directly isolate the asked person's variable) using algebraic elimination, substitution, or matrix methods; never guess without calculation.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Once every relevant tomato statement has been converted into an equation and all transfers have been applied.
mathgap.example: Listing dozens of equations and then outputting 'The final answer is \boxed{1}' without performing any algebraic solution.

mathgap.description: Treating direct count statements as final counts after transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes the given explicit numbers already include the effect of later transfers, ignoring the need to apply transfers first.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret explicit counts as initial amounts; apply all transfer updates before using those counts in any relational equation.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses the giver and receiver, adding to the giver instead of subtracting.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a statement says 'X gives N to Y', subtract N from X and add N to Y.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops the order of subtraction and treats differences as non‑negative magnitudes.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the order: 'difference between A and B' means A − B, not |A − B|.

mathgap.description: Applying relational equations before applying transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model uses equations that involve final counts while still working with pre‑transfer values.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: First process all transfer statements to obtain updated counts, then formulate and solve relational equations.

mathgap.description: Incomplete solving: failing to derive the answer from the constraints, leading to a guess
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model enumerates many equations but stops without performing algebraic elimination, resorting to an arbitrary answer.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: After all equations are set up, actually solve the linear system (or isolate the target variable) using substitution, elimination, or matrix methods; verify the answer satisfies all constraints.
